close_reason: Resolved by 13d3253 (JMAP-ly0n.15): the README's promised shape {type_name, payload} is now the actual code shape. The README/code mismatch is closed by aligning the code, not the docs (matching the README's preservation-policy intent per workspace AGENTS.md §6).
description:
Trigger: a downstream consumer reads the README of jmap-chat-types and writes a match arm for EphemeralMessage::Unknown { type_name, payload }.

Bad behavior: code does not compile, because in crate-jmap-chat-types/src/ephemeral.rs:122-124 the Unknown variant is a unit variant attached via #[serde(other)]:

    /// Any `@type` not recognized by this version of the library.
    #[serde(other)]
    Unknown,

But crate-jmap-chat-types/README.md:97 promises:

    EphemeralMessage::Unknown { type_name, payload }
    ... Callers must handle this variant; match exhaustion without it will not compile.

Two real consequences:
1. The README claim that the unknown variant carries the type-name and payload is false. As written, the raw payload of an unknown @type is dropped on deserialize — there is no round-trip preservation for unknown EphemeralMessage variants. Compare to ChatKind / DeliveryState / ReadDisposition which carry Other(String) and round-trip the wire value verbatim.
2. The README's claim about non-compiling match arms is technically true (Unknown is a variant), but for the wrong reason and with the wrong shape.

Fix: pick one and align both:
(a) keep the unit variant but rewrite the README to match (and accept the loss-of-payload trade), OR
(b) reshape Unknown to a struct variant that captures the unknown @type and payload (requires a custom Deserialize impl since #[serde(other)] doesn't support carrying the discriminant). Option (b) matches the rest of the crate's 'preserve everything' policy and matches the README claim.

Priority P1: documentation lies about behavior, but the actual deserialize path doesn't panic, it silently drops. This is exactly the kind of thing the workspace extras-preservation policy was meant to prevent — losing data because the type model can't represent it. The fact that Section 6 of the workspace AGENTS.md spends ~50 lines on extras-preservation as 'workspace policy is preservation' makes EphemeralMessage::Unknown's silent-drop a policy gap worth closing.
title: README documents EphemeralMessage::Unknown as struct variant; code defines it as unit variant
